newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Korea prepared to await China decision on defector.
newsitem.headline: Korea prepared to await China decision on defector.

text.p: South Korea suggested on Saturday it was prepared to go along with Chinas decision to take its time in deciding how to resolve a diplomatic crisis over a top North Korean defector in Seouls Beijing embassy.
"I think we have started a good discussion with China and we have to wait and see," South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha told reporters.
"I dont think that its right now to make any judgment on this," when asked how soon a decision would be made on defector Hwang Jang-yop, who was ranked 24th in Pyongyangs hierarchy.
Yoo was in Singapore for a meeting of 25 Asian and European foreign ministers and had talks Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen on Friday.
"We have discussed this matter and I have conveyed that request of my government that China accommodate the free will of Mr Hwang and allow him to leave, maybe on humanitarian grounds," Yoo added.
Qian said after meeting Yoo that the defection -- which North Korea says is a kidnap -- had taken China by surprise and it needed time to investigate the incident.
Hwangs defection on Wednesday -- South Korea says he took a taxi to its Beijing embassy and asked for asylum -- is a problem for China.

If it decides to let him go to Seoul, it offends old socialist comrade North Korea. If it sends him back to Pyongyang and possible execution, it upsets South Korea, a major investor in its booming economy.
Hwang, 73, was a pillar of North Koreas Stalinist establishment and a senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.
